title: Brahma searches for the source and begins creation
arc: Brahma awakens on the navel lotus and searches downward for its source; after returning to meditate, he beholds Narayana resting on Adishesha, praises him, receives the capacity and instruction to create, undertakes further tapas, and begins the three worlds and beings.

scene_brief.mode: Brahma turns in wonder on the navel lotus
must_show: One Brahma seated on the fully opened lotus attached by one continuous stem to Narayana’s navel; Brahma turns his gaze around the directions in wonder.
Brahma has exactly four heads total, with three faces visible from the frontal view and the fourth head turned behind, and exactly four separate, attached arms and hands.

If Narayana’s body is visible, show exactly four attached arms; viewer-left upper hand holds a discus, viewer-right upper hand holds a conch, viewer-left lower hand holds a lotus, viewer-right lower hand holds a mace. Keep all four hands distinct and connected.
The lotus rises above calm causal water; no extra people or duplicate Brahma forms.
scene_brief.composition: Compose a single wide scene with the reclining Lord low in frame, the long lotus stem clearly rooted at his navel, and Brahma large enough on the lotus to read three frontal faces and four arms. Keep every head, hand, and attribute inside safe margins.
avoid: gloss, metallic gold, cinematic beams, text, watermark, outer border
scene_brief.source_summary: Seated on the lotus at Narayana’s navel, Brahma looks in every direction and becomes four-faced, with eight lotus-like eyes.
scene_brief.reference_mapping: 001.jpg and caption #1 show Brahma seated on the navel lotus, turning outward; they support the ordinal match. The reference's polished cosmic treatment and hand details are not instructions.

stanzas.alt: Brahma turns in wonder on the navel lotus.

landscape.composition_override: Compose natively as a wide scene; leave space around all four heads, arms, and the lotus stem.

portrait.composition_override: Portrait production is paused; do not crop or extend the landscape.

Brahma does not find Narayana; depict the hollow interior as a simple continuous passage, not a second scene or a cutaway panel.

A single Brahma on his lotus witnesses the vision with wonder and contentment. Brahma has four heads total, three distinct visible frontal faces with the fourth turned behind, and exactly four attached arms; two lower palms join in reverence, upper viewer-left holds a closed blank scripture bundle, and upper viewer-right holds prayer beads.
The inner vision is a single connected tableau; no Lakshmi, extra worshippers, repeated Brahma, floating detached serpent coils, or other deity figures.

scene_brief.mode: Brahma praises the Lord and asks for creative intelligence
must_show: One Brahma praises the Lord after beholding him and asks for the intelligence needed to create the worlds.

Brahma has four heads total, three distinct faces visible from the front and the fourth turned behind, and exactly four attached arms. The lower pair join in praise; the upper pair are separately open in supplication, with no objects obscuring attachment.

Narayana has exactly four attached arms: upper viewer-left (his right) holds discus, upper viewer-right (his left) holds conch, lower viewer-left (his right) is raised in assurance, lower viewer-right (his left) rests open on the knee. All hands are clear and distinct.
Use one figure of each deity; no Bhattathiri, extra devotees, or repeated temporal version.
scene_brief.composition: A clear two-figure wide devotional encounter, with Brahma at left on the lotus and Narayana to the right on Adishesha or a simple cosmic seat. Leave space between their silhouettes so no hands or arms fuse.
avoid: repeated Brahma heads arranged as separate bodies
gloss, metallic surfaces, decorative border, text, watermark
scene_brief.source_summary: Brahma praises the Lord whose majesty is revealed in scripture and asks him to make Brahma's intelligence capable of creating the worlds.
scene_brief.reference_mapping: 007.jpg and caption #7 show the two principal figures in a praise/teaching encounter; the paper-like marks in the reference are not to be reproduced. Handedness clarification: supplied D009 006.jpg and 007.jpg place Narayana’s discus on the viewer-left upper arm, his anatomical right; the adjacent conch belongs on the viewer-right upper arm. The scene contract states this explicitly in viewer space while retaining its exact four-arm count and required lower-hand actions. The source image 007.jpg places the discus in Narayana’s upper hand on viewer-left, establishing that his anatomical right side appears on viewer-left. To keep “right” anatomical and avoid a mirrored gesture, the lower assurance hand is assigned to that same viewer-left side; the left hand rests on the viewer-right knee. This changes only side wording, not count or action.

stanzas.alt: Brahma praises the Lord and asks for creative intelligence.

Brahma has exactly four heads total, three frontal faces and a fourth turned behind, plus exactly four attached arms; two lower hands rest distinctly in his lap, upper right holds prayer beads, upper left is open in joyful acceptance.
